LESSON: BELIEF IN HIS

Grade: PP1
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.2: Belief in His

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Belief in His. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain what Belief in His means in simple pupil language
2. give 3 correct examples of Belief in His from Kenya
3. practise Belief in His in clear steps
4. apply Belief in His in one real-life situation this week

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: BELIEF IN HIS
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: PP1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Belief in His helps you succeed in ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: BELIEF IN HIS
Study Belief in His like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Explain what Belief in His means in simple pupil language

What this means
In this part you learn to explain what Belief in His means in simple pupil language. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain what Belief in His means in simple pupil language.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Belief in His” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain what Belief in His means in simple pupil language. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Give 3 correct examples of Belief in His from Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to give 3 correct examples of Belief in His from Kenya. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: give 3 correct examples of Belief in His from Kenya.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Belief in His in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can give 3 correct examples of Belief in His from Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Practise Belief in His in clear steps

What this means
In this part you learn to practise Belief in His in clear steps. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise Belief in His in clear steps.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise Belief in His in clear steps. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Apply Belief in His in one real-life situation this week

What this means
In this part you learn to apply Belief in His in one real-life situation this week. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply Belief in His in one real-life situation this week.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Belief in His” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply Belief in His in one real-life situation this week. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Belief in His is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Belief in His” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: explain what Belief in His means in simple pupil language)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Belief in His in your own words. (skill: give 3 correct examples of Belief in His from Kenya)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: practise Belief in His in clear steps)

Example 4: Show how “Belief in His” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: apply Belief in His in one real-life situation this week)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Belief in His to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain what Belief in His means in simple pupil language.
3. Practise this skill: give 3 correct examples of Belief in His from Kenya.
4. Practise this skill: practise Belief in His in clear steps.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Belief in His from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Belief in His: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP1 learner study Belief in His?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Belief in His means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain what Belief in His means in simple pupil language.
5. Be able to: give 3 correct examples of Belief in His from Kenya.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
